Lena: Ran a bunch of perf + nsys traces on the warmup hiccup customers reported this morning. attaching key notes.

Lena: TL;DR: two distinct CPU hotspots — tokenizer wakeups and the scheduler spin path during kernel fallback. KV cache churn amplifies the scheduler sidewall.

Lena: Perf command I used: `perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60` then `perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded` and `flamegraph.pl out.folded > perf.svg`

Lena: Quick flame snippet (top stacks):
```
  run_worker_loop
  scheduler::poll_batch
  batching::check_wakeup
  py::call_function
  tokenize::split_on_whitespace
```

Max: Interesting — tokenizer appears in user stacks not syscalls. likely Python-level cost, not libc. did you capture a pstack or annotated python symbols?

Lena: Yup, I did a python-symbols-enabled build. The flame shows long thin stacks in `tokenize::split_on_whitespace` and `py::unicode_split` for medium requests (seq len ~512).

Priya: Could the tokenizer be suffering from repeated allocations because of KV cache misses? i remember we re-copy input for each new batch when cache empty.

Lena: Exactly. On cold KV cache the prefix isn't shared so each request goes through tokenization + prefix concatenation. I measured ~12% CPU per tokenization at peak.

Zoe: On the scheduler side what did nsys show? any kernel stalls or futex spam?

Lena: nsys GPU timeline was clean. CPU timeline (perf + perfetto) shows lots of short runnable states in the scheduler thread, correlated with fallback kernel selection decisions. There is a tight loop that checks `kernel_availability()` and calls `choose_fallback()` which spins for ~1-2ms before yielding.

Lena: Minimal repro snippet from the trace (pseudo):
```
while (!kernel_ready) {
  if (try_select_optimized_kernel()) break;
  usleep(50); // but sometimes falls into spin path
  spin_wait(200); // exponential backoff missing here
}
```

Max: So two issues: (1) tokenizer doing heavy Python work on every request during warmup; (2) scheduler uses a spin-y path when kernels transiently unavailable. combined -> hiccup.

Priya: For tokenizer: can we move split to C++ and reuse buffers on the pool? that should drop the CPU and reduce GIL hold time.

Lena: I prototyped `fast_split` in C++ and saw tokenization drop ~3.5x in microbench. But we need to be careful about Unicode corner cases.

Zoe: For scheduler: propose changing fallback logic to event-driven -> add a condition variable to sleep until kernel state changes instead of spin. Also add a short randomized jitter to avoid thundering herd.

Lena: Agreed. Also added a quick interim mitigation: prefer `fallback_variant` routing earlier (route to lower-cost kernel) when KV cache miss rate > 30% so scheduler doesn't keep probing heavy kernels. In traces that dropped the scheduler spin by ~60%.

Max: Any regression signals? did this previously pass perf CI?

Lena: The perf CI didn't cover warmup-case because put synthetic steady-state load. This is specifically warmup/cold-cache. I added a new perf-smoke that runs short cold-start bursts; local run catches regression.

Priya: Can we add a small cache-warmup prefetch on route selection? e.g., when we see new model version or cold cache, spawn a low-priority prefetcher to populate KV for top prefixes.

Lena: I implemented a prototype: prefetcher uses prioritized queue and `io_uring` backend, pre-populates KV for top N prefixes seen in logs. It reduced tokenization hits on traces by ~40%.

Zoe: Nice. Anything for observability so oncall can see this at-a-glance?

Lena: Added two metrics: `warmup_tokenization_cpu_pct` and `scheduler_spin_ms_per_minute`. Dashboard draft in console under perf/ops -> warmup. Also alert if tokenization CPU > 10% for > 1m on a node.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: canary build with C++ tokenizer and event-driven scheduler will roll to staging at 02:15 UTC unless blocked. :rocket:

Max: One more note — kernel selection logs were noisy. Add a sampling log level so we don't flood disks.

Lena: Will add `kernel_select: sample=0.1` and `warmup_prefetch: enabled=true` flags to runtime config.

Priya: Could you drop the prototype PR and the perf traces in the ticket? I'll review and look at Unicode tests.

Lena: PR + perf traces uploaded to issue #4723. attaching perf.svg and nsys timeline slices.

Zoe: Thanks — getting closer. After staging run let's measure p95 latency and token throughput for cold-start burst (10 concurrent requests, seq 512) and compare to baseline.

Lena: Will run those and post numbers here. next update ~ 1945679175.

Lena: update: staging run shows p95 latency down from 420ms -> 260ms on cold bursts, CPU variance reduced. leaving traces in the ticket. :thumbsup:
